**Conversation Overview**

This conversation continued an ongoing technical project called "The Method 1.6" Phase R2, a systematic review and verification effort involving a complex lattice-based formal system. The person's role appears to be author/reviewer of a technical manuscript, and Claude served as an automated analysis assistant executing a structured protocol across multiple chat sessions. The session was chat 85 in a long sequence, picking up from a handoff document (HANDOFF-37) left by chat 84.

The work followed a strict cadence established in earlier sessions: gate verification of bundle integrity, section reading with claim census, computable and prose instrument batches, findings documentation, and handoff preparation. The gate passed for BUILD112/BUILD90 bundles (330 members, all checksums verified). The section read covered main document §16.6–§16.8 (lines 4482–4788, 307 lines, sixteen subsections). Two instrument batches were written, run, and banked: r2-ch13p (computable, ~93 seconds) and r2-ch13q (prose, ~1 second). Thirteen deviations, ten verified findings, and ten incidental observations were documented in READ-ch13p.md. A long-deferred cross-chapter item (the ⅅ_gro/multiverse attribution from chat 74) was closed as a confirmed defect. BUILD113 was produced (4,076,805 B, md5 580489a6…, 334 members), HANDOFF-38 was written, and three files were delivered to outputs.

Key domain terminology includes: Λ₈ (a 976-cell lattice), amplification A(y), thermometer bit-packing, sublattice closure, join/meet irreducibles, step operator, pushback, ℛ (box sweep operator), fibre, descendants table, and a seven-constraint directed dependency graph over atomic spectroscopy coordinates (n, ℓ, k, q, e, f, g, 2S). The project tracks numbered defect classes (e.g., 13p-01 through 13p-13) and maintains strict discipline: timeout on every call, no member editing in place, delete-only pycache calls kept separate from banking operations, and no corrections or register entries until the review closes.

**Tool Knowledge**

Google Drive searches used `title contains 'BUILD113_compendia' or title contains 'BUILD90_main'` with `pageSize=5` and `excludeContentSnippets=True`; results spill to `/mnt/user-data/tool_results/<toolu_id>.json` and must be decoded via `json.loads(json.load(open(path))[0]['text'])['content']` before base64 decoding with `validate=True`. A 32-bit lookup table indexed by thermometer codes requires ~31.9 GiB and must be replaced with a compact mixed-radix index of size 16,384. The `np.isin` approach with `assume_unique=True` is reliable for frontier-based closure; `np.add.at` handles pushback counting without race conditions. Bundle extraction uses the `<<<FILE: name>>>\n...\n<<<END FILE: name>>>` delimiter pattern with `re.S|re.M` flags.

## Chat 85 — Phase R2, §16.6–§16.8: work so far

**Gate PASS.** 330 members extracted, both md5s asserted (main `49065309…` / BUILD112 `89e1b72a…`), census byte-identical, core five OK, MANIFEST 329/330, chat 84's two instruments OK, `GATE-ch85 verdict PASS`. RULINGS-R2.md and DEFERRED.md read, chat 84's block last.

**Boundaries re-verified by heading scan (MEASURED):** §16.6 opens L4482, Chapter 17 opens L4789 — HANDOFF-37 is correct. 307 lines, sixteen subsections, read whole in two calls.

**Computable batch `r2-ch13p` banked** — 9,543 B, md5 `30e7afea`, 148 lines, 93 s.

### The findings that carry

**A floor of 59 that the figure on the same page contradicts.** §16.8.4 L4692 prints "minimum 59 across 220 trials" and the table at L4703 prints "amplifies, always — minimum 59". Measured over the **population** (all 5,936 cells of the ambient box outside Λ₈): minimum **15**, median **309**, 86 cells below 59, zero free insertions. The 59 is exactly the minimum over the *2S ≤ k* class alone — a class minimum printed as the global floor. Figure 16.2's caption eleven lines later prints minimum **15**, which is right; its median 352 and the body's 340 both measure 309.

**φ(2S | k) = 1 at k = 1 is false as printed** (§16.8.1 L4665). Measured: 2S ∈ {0, 1}, φ = **2**. The conclusion stands — the cell asks 2S = 2 and is refused — but the stated fibre is wrong. The 13g-01 class.

**The self-count.** The heading says six; the table below it lists **seven** rows; the next sentence says "the first four cannot reach the last three" — also seven. The 13j-11 class, now in Chapter 16.

**§16.7.4's "§16.3's five recorded failures":** §16.3 and §16.3.1 record one worked case; §16.7.4's own table lists three.

**§16.8.6 L4786 "they agree on Λ and nowhere else"** — its own table prints 74/74 on Λ ∪ {y}, and measurement gives agreement on 30/30 of the 2S ≤ k violators and 30/30 of g ≤ q.

**The A/fibre model does not reproduce.** "Fibre" is defined nowhere in the section. Two readings swept: under the violator-count reading, ℓ≤n−1 gives 0.386 (printed 0.39 ✓) and k≤4ℓ+2 gives 0.477 (printed 0.48 ✓), but all three descendants-0 rows fail their 0.96–0.99 band, and corr(descendants, A/fibre) measures +0.284 and +0.819 against a printed −0.942.

### Verified exactly (Section B)

The fabrication: 976 → **1,051**, A = **74**, **75** added cells all breaking 2S ≤ k, closed under join and meet, E = 0, a fixed point of ℛ. Pushback: **475,800** pairs, min **16**, mean **739.0**, max **5,091**, zero removable (median measures 503 against a printed 504). Eighteen join-irreducibles, eighteen meet-irreducibles, **intersection empty**. step(Λ₈) = **4**, interval (2,1,3,3,2,1,3,0)–(3,1,3,3,3,1,3,0), free in **n and e**, 972 cells, **471,906** surviving pairs — and the interval's lower endpoint is the least-pushed cell. **16** binding pairs, exactly the transitive closure of the seven defining edges, whose transitive reduction returns those seven. The full descendants table (0,0,0,1,1,3,4) matches every row.

### Open at this point

`r2-ch13q.py` (prose batch) is written but **not yet run or banked**. Still owed for the close: run and bank r2-ch13q, write READ-ch13p.md and CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch13p.tsv, W-123, BUILD113 via close.py, HANDOFF-38. The DEFERRED `ⅅ_gro` item is resolved in substance — §14.6.1 L4115–4116 attributes to §16.6 a grading of *multiverse dimension* that §16.6 does not perform; §16.6's only ⅅ_gro instance is *q*, called "the one with no instance anywhere until now" — but the grep confirmation is in the unrun batch and is INFERRED until it runs.

Context is at roughly 80–85% (INFERRED). The section read is not closed, so the cadence forbids a handoff here — the next step is to run and bank r2-ch13q and close the section.

- Governing members (read at every open): `RULINGS-R2.md` (rulings, append-only), `DEFERRED.md` (cross-chapter items, append-only; do not re-derive), the READ-chNN.md members and W-101… in WORKING-REGISTER.md (findings; never restated in handoffs).

## 4. Rulings in force

- Chat 67: every volume read in full, no editing until the review closes.
- Chat 68: instruments travel as bundle members; the gate fetches the two bundles from Drive by title; Drive is the store.
- Chat 69: handoff at 90–95 % or on a closed segment.
- Chat 70 (R1): CENSUS-CLOSURES-A governs its 21 shared rows; A vocabulary (*defect / not a defect*) in every closure file; an unreferenced prior-art row is a defect; co-located stale text counts against its census row.
- Chat 72: begin the close when the remaining context would not fit a segment plus the build; record the estimate.
- Chat 74: (1) no direct bundle uploads — Drive remains the store; (2) the gate and the close are instruments (gate.py, close.py, r2lib.py, banked NAME.out goldens); (3) the handoff carries identity, bootstrap, run list, next work, Drive actions and the prompt; rulings live in RULINGS-R2.md and deferred items in DEFERRED.md.
- M's priorities: the computational audits are paramount; every stated value is recomputed; stale self-description and production classes are noted, not a concern.
- Earlier rulings still governing the books: Ruling 29 (the only Register edit class: pointer removal), 38 (the Register's front matter is a purpose statement only), 41 (false carried state is discarded without refutation), 45 (no build or editorial-process remarks in any reader-facing volume), 46 (no script names, build numbers or internal file references visible to readers), 56 (Prints & Proofs as original-input witness), W-101 (all subject matter completely true and proven).

## 5. Standing discipline (gates G0…)

- **Measure from files, never recite.** Grep every line number before it is written. Label every claim MEASURED (with the command), INFERRED, or record-carried; inferences are never carried into a handoff as fact.
- **No silent change.** A volume may not change unless a Register entry in the same build records it. Every edit is a measured diff with count-asserted substitutions and a reverse-md5 guard; build.py's SUBS six-way split is the preferred discriminator (G0x).
- **Register entries are append-only** — never removed, relocated or renumbered; a superseded entry is corrected by a new entry that cites it; both states are preserved. Moving an entry out is a deletion.
- **When a reconstruction disagrees with the record, the finding is about the reconstruction.** Never withdraw a recorded finding on reconstructed evidence without the original instrument. Never change an instrument to make a discrepancy disappear (G0c).
- **Authorised work is reported done or not done;** a shortfall is named explicitly. Silence is not completion.
- A message containing a question ends at the question mark; the next action is never announced in the same message as a question (G0, highest priority). Rulings are compact numbered lists and take effect without re-explanation.
- A defect line and its disposition are different objects; the later line governs (G0b). Re-test defects from the file, never from prior dispositions. Measure in the pressed PDF, not simulation (G0aa); census figures at press, not at source (G0w). A docket's target is a hypothesis until read and measured (G0v).
- A command that deletes does nothing else (G0e). Never hand-transcribe base64. `validate=True` on every b64decode. Simulate sweep order before asserting anchor uniqueness (G0q). "Registers N" cites and is counted by register_cites.py; "entries N" merely names (G0i).
- `timeout 280` on every call. Never copy over an existing file; list a directory before copying. Never edit a seated member in place (append-only members grow only through close.py `--append`). Remove `members/__pycache__` (delete-only call) before any census or build and after every instrument run.
- Shell is dash: text goes through python heredocs or create_file; no `<(…)`; one heredoc per call; non-ASCII grep output through python. Import tower-2.py by path via r2lib.load_tower(), never by copying.
- Instruments print no wall-clock time (goldens must be deterministic); an instrument over ~200 s is trimmed. Functions owed to r2lib are copied verbatim into the new instrument with a provenance comment until lifted (DEFERRED lists them).
- C7/C9 census rows whose flagged token is a live figure, label, or the cited section's own claim are regex artefacts (precedents 678, 680–687, 1067, 1069).

## 6. Session shape

1. **§0 gate**, each step its own call: list directories; `recent_chats` confirms the latest chat; fetch both bundles by title (`title contains 'BUILDNNN_compendia' or title contains 'BUILD90_main'`, pageSize 5, excludeContentSnippets); bootstrap from the spill files with the handoff's script (assert md5s; extract members); `gate.py census`; `gate.py run --core`; `gate.py manifest`; `gate.py run` on the previous chat's instruments; `gate.py cert NN`. Any FAIL stops the chat with a report.
2. Read RULINGS-R2.md and DEFERRED.md from the members.
3. **Segments:** one or two subsections each. `r2-tools.py lines|pointers|figures|census|layout A B` (pointer regex is case-sensitive and ignores Appendix A item numbers — grep lowercase `register NNN` and `A.N` by hand); read every line; resolve every pointer to heading AND claim; grep every figure; re-measure every tower-computable claim on all cells or pairs in `members/r2-chNN.py` importing r2lib by path; write READ-chNN.md (A deviations with both texts; B verified; C incidental) and CENSUS-CLOSURES-chNN.tsv (id, verdict, reason; header only when no row is in range); bank the golden with `gate.py bank`.
4. **Close:** W-NNN.md (begins `### W-NNN —`, ends with a blank line; gate, segments, close estimate); `close.py --old … --new … --w … [--append DEFERRED.md …] --members …` (reverse must recover the old md5); HANDOFF-NN+1 in the current handoff's form; copy to outputs without overwriting; present the handoff first, then the build and the READ files; closing report of done / not done / M's Drive actions.

## 7. Content standards for the books

- All subject matter completely true and proven; every figure computed on the rebuilt lattice before authoring.
- Compendium entries follow R-FORM: descriptive title → bold dense headline with §-pointers on first mention → italic scope-caps line → Proved/Computed + citation chain → blockquote Prior art. All attributions that can be made are made (R-ATTR).
- No object handles or workshop jargon in reader-facing volumes; cross-references name the object by its descriptive title with a source pointer on first mention per entry. Image captions state facts only.
- The compendium standard: comprehensive scope without filler; intuitive taxonomy with a robust index; consistent formatting; concise synthesis; unified voice; strict fact-checking; fluid cross-referencing; dual-purpose accessibility; clear visual hierarchy. Compendium canon order is the main volume's physical order; reordering and renumbering is a last step executed once after all subject matter is settled.
- kinds.py's table is recomputed after any Register entry addition; extent ("1 to NNNN") restated everywhere.

## 8. Response style

- Focused and brief; caveats short; the bulk of the response is the answer; high-level unless depth was requested. Cover the substance; skip boilerplate and redundant summaries.
- Scope rule: deliver what was asked; raise a better approach in one sentence; then proceed as asked.
- Delegation rule: large independent work only, never for self-verification, low spawn counts.
- Keep internal or system tags out of responses. Rulings are given back as numbered lists.

## 9. Tools and quirks

- Drive: large files spill to `/mnt/user-data/tool_results/<id>.json`; decode with `base64.b64decode(json.loads(json.load(open(p))[0]['text'])['content'], validate=True)`. Small files arrive inline (quoted heredoc, strip, same decode). Hard cap ≈ 10 MB. `read_file_content` mangles indentation — never for code. `parentId = '<id>'` with excludeContentSnippets lists a folder.
- Bundle member extraction: `^<<<FILE: (.+?)>>>\n(.*?)<<<END FILE: \1>>>\n` with `re.S|re.M` on the decoded bytes; members of both bundles into one `/home/claude/members/`.
- Build pipeline: Markdown → pandoc → LibreOffice → docx/pdf; `pdftotext -layout` drops table rows — confirm through docx XML.
- Key instruments: tower-2.py, lam8.py, build.py, kinds.py, register_cites.py, appf.py, index_pages.py, coords.py, bundle.py, split.py, gate.py, close.py, r2lib.py, r2-tools.py, census.py, minmax.py.

4482	### 16.6 The defences are disjoint, and there are six
  4483	  mechanism        catches                                              worked case
  4484	  ℛ(Λ) = Λ         rules not recoverable from cells                     periodic table, E = 36
  4485	  ⅅ≥1              a wrong value in data or derivation                  wrong Z; w = 3ν·e
  4486	  χ_Λ total        a missing value coerced to a real one                the cap discard
  4487	
  4488	 **Three was the count while every defence was built from the object. There are six, and the other
  4489	 three reach a coordinate this book does not carry: what a term refers to.**
  4490	
  4491	  mechanism        catches                                        runnable by the book
  4492	  ℛ(Λ) = Λ         rules not recoverable from cells               yes
  4493	  ⅅ ≥ 1            a wrong value in data or derivation            yes
  4494	  χ_Λ total        a missing value coerced to a real one          yes
  4495	  §28.8's index    a choice that depended on its answer           yes
  4496	  **ⅅ_ref**        **a term meaning one thing here and another in the theorem it was borrowed from**   **no — the verdict must be read**
  4497	  **ⅅ_dict**       **drift away from a referent already established**                                  **yes, given the referent**
  4498	  **ⅅ_gro**        **a term with no referent at all**                                                  **yes, once the term is placed**
  4499	
  4500	 **Why the first four cannot reach the last three.** All four compare the book against the book. A
  4501	 conflation is not a disagreement between two places in this book; it is an *agreement* between the
  4502	 book and itself about a word doing different work elsewhere. Twenty-one structural audits passed on
  4503	 a companion document carrying five of them.
  4504	
  4505	 **ⅅ_ref and ⅅ_dict are not the same mechanism at two strengths.** Establishing a referent requires
  4506	 reading someone else's theorem and is not runnable. *Maintaining* one is mechanical: once a
  4507	 coordinate carries a stated referent, checking that every later use is consistent with it is a
  4508	 computation. ⅅ_ref is paid once per coordinate; ⅅ_dict runs forever after. The tower's 2K is the
  4509	 worked case — it means J_c + ℓ_outer in jK, L_total + S_core in LK, and jj has no K at all, and
  4510	 Racah's recoupling coefficients translate between them exactly.
  4511	
  4512	 **ⅅ_gro is the one with no instance anywhere until now.** *q*, this book's transfer coordinate, has
  4513	 no referent in the spectroscopic literature — not conflated, since there is nothing to conflate
  4514	 with. ⅅ_ref cannot see it: if no theorem names the term, the pair never enters the table.
  4515	
  4516	 **And the three repairs are already named, in the companion paper, without being named as
  4517	 defences**: SPLIT for a conflation, DICTIONARY for one meaning in two bases, TRANSLATOR for a
  4518	 referent that must be manufactured. Register 403.
  4519	
  4520	### 16.6.1 The vocabulary of reference, as an index
  4521	
  4522	 The three new mechanisms need a vocabulary this book does not have: its back-matter Index carries
  4523	 fifty-one terms and **not one of them says what a term points at**. Defined here on the same
  4524	 discipline as every other index in this book — ordered coordinates, one categorical fibre,
  4525	 constraints of §16.4 form.
  4526	
  4527	  coordinate   values
  4528	  access       blocked < secondary < abstract < full text
  4529	  referent     none < named < named with its stated hypothesis
  4530	  checked      not checked < against one theorem < against every theorem naming it
  4531	  verdict      undetermined < conflated < partial < match
  4532	
  4533	 fibred by **kind** — coordinate · equation · source · result. *Repair* — none, dictionary, split,
  4534	 translator — is **not a coordinate**: it is a function of verdict and referent, and §17.2's Theorem 17.1
  4535	 forbids one — adjunction never repairs. It is read off.
  4536	
  4537	 **38 cells, ambient box 144, density 26.4%, E = 0** — the densest object in this book after the
  4538	 periodic table. **And it is not a tree**: access bounds *referent at its top value* and bounds
  4539	 *checked* directly, closing the cycle access–referent–checked. Width 2, so Freuder cannot be
  4540	 inherited and the zero above is a computation rather than a certificate — §12.11.0.4's Λ₉′ arriving
  4541	 in the vocabulary rather than in the lattice.
  4542	
  4543	 **Applied to twenty-eight load-bearing terms of this book and its companion: thirteen cells
  4544	 occupied of thirty-eight, E = 11.** One term with no referent, eight named and never checked, nine
  4545	 checked and conflated, two partial, eight matching, four capped by a blocked source. **Sixty-eight
  4546	 per cent have been checked at all.**
  4547	
  4548	 **One constraint was withdrawn during construction and the withdrawal is the finding.** The index
  4549	 first required a named referent to have a reachable source, and refused four cells the book
  4550	 occupies — Edlén 1964, Ritz 1908, Paschen & Götze 1922, Dunz 1911. §19.5 already says otherwise:
  4551	 *a blocked ρ = 1 cell is a stated gap, not an unexplained absence.* Naming a referent and reading
  4552	 one are different acts. Totality forbade rather than detected, exactly as §16.5 says it does, and
  4553	 what it forbade located the wrong constraint. Register 404.
  4554	
  4555	### 16.6.2 And one coordinate sits below this book's own floor
  4556	
  4557	 §16.1 gives ⅅ ≥ 1 as the condition under which an index can check itself, and every defence in this
  4558	 book rests on it. **The reference index has one coordinate for which ⅅ = 0, permanently.**
  4559	
  4560	 Three of its four coordinates are internal: *access*, *referent* and *checked* are all recordable
  4561	 from this book's own pages. **Verdict is not.** It requires reading someone else's theorem, and the
  4562	 index that supplies it is the bibliography — for which §29.1 already proves ⅅ(novelty) = 0,
  4563	 necessarily and permanently, because search is one route and can never be two.
  4564	
  4565	    ⅅ(bibliography) = 0 ⟹ ⅅ(verdict) = 0, inherited.
  4566	
  4567	 **So the reference debt is not unpayable because sources are blocked.** Blocked access caps four of
  4568	 twenty-eight terms at a lower level. The undefendability of *verdict* caps all twenty-eight, and it
  4569	 is the first coordinate anywhere in this book below the ⅅ ≥ 1 floor the rest of Chapter 16 stands
  4570	 on. Register 405.
  4571	
  4572	 **No mechanism catches another's class**, and this work supplied an instance of each.
  4573	
  4574	### 16.7 Two kinds of absence, and one kind of lie
  4575	 An index can be wrong in two ways, and they are not alike. One it can detect by itself. The
  4576	 other it cannot detect at all.
  4577	
  4578	### 16.7.1 A missing cell — and the index can tell whether the gap is real
  4579	 E(X) > 0 says the structure admits cells the collection does not hold. It does not say why, and
  4580	 there are two reasons:
  4581	
  4582	    the gap is an artefact of the layout — a property of how the index was drawn the gap is a fact
  4583	    about the world — nothing occupies that cell because nothing can
  4584	
  4585	 **And the index distinguishes them, by asking whether E is removable.**
  4586	
  4587	| the periodic table | E |
  4588	|---|---|
  4589	| 18-column | **36** |
  4590	| 32-column | 106 |
  4591	| **Janet left-step** | **0** |
  4592	
  4593	 **The same 118 elements. Order the blocks f, d, p, s and define the period by *n* + ℓ, and the defect vanishes.** So the 36 belong to the drawing.
  4594	
  4595	 Now the same test on a catalogue where the absences are physical. Index the mean-motion
  4596	 resonances by (p, q), reduced, with the order p − q derived rather than made an axis, and give ℛ only
  4597	 the resonances that show structure in the asteroid belt:
  4598	
  4599	| the belt | E |
  4600	|---|---|
  4601	| (*p*, *q*) | 2 |
  4602	| (order, *p*) | 1 |
  4603	| (*p*, order) | 1 |
  4604	
  4605	    E is irreducible, and ℛ refuses all six absences outright — 0 of 6 admitted, against 36 of
  4606	    36 admitted for the periodic table.
  4607	
  4608	 And the physics confirms what the index inferred without being told it. Every resonance of order
  4609	 ≤ 7 in the belt is occupied; every one of order ≥ 8 is empty. Thirteen of thirteen above the cut, zero
  4610	
  4611	 of six below. Resonance strength enters at e^\|p−q\|, so the absences are exponentially weak and
  4612	 genuinely unoccupied.
  4613	
  4614	    A defect of the index vanishes under some re-coordinatisation. A feature of the world
  4615	    survives every one. The test is computable from the cells alone, and §6.2's Janet table is that test
  4616	    — run once, on one example, and never named as one.
  4617	
  4618	### 16.7.2 A complete index of something that is not there
  4619	 The second failure is different in kind, and no re-coordinatisation touches it.
  4620	
  4621	 Insert one impossible cell — **one electron with spin multiplicity 2, which no atom has** — and let the closure supply everything that follows. The result:
  4622	
  4623	                                                                     Λ            the fabrication
  4624	  cells                                                              976          1,051
  4625	  closed under join and meet                                         true         true
  4626	  E(X)                                                               0            0
  4627	  fixed point of ℛ                                                   true         true
  4628	
  4629	 **And E stays 0 for both under every re-coordinatisation tested.** The test of §16.7.1 has nothing to work on:
  4630	
  4631	    that test finds missing cells and asks whether the gap is real. A coherent fabrication has
  4632	    no missing cells. It is full.
  4633	
  4634	 **The fabrication contains 75 configurations no atom can have**, and the structure records nothing about it. Every law in this book certifies it.
  4635	
  4636	### 16.7.3 The plain version
  4637	    A defective index is a map with a street missing. You catch it by redrawing — the street
  4638	    reappears in another projection. A coherent fabrication is a complete, consistent map of a
  4639	    city that does not exist. Every street connects, every distance adds up. Redrawing changes
  4640	    nothing, because nothing is missing.
  4641	
  4642	 **The only thing that distinguishes a map of a real city from a perfect map of an imaginary one is going there.** In this book, going there means measuring a level.
  4643	
  4644	### 16.7.4 Which is what D_phys is for, and only that
  4645	 §16.3's five recorded failures are all of the second kind. Not one is a missing cell.
  4646	
  4647	| failure | what it does |
  4648	|---|---|
  4649	| a wrong nuclear charge | every derived value shifts **together**; the index stays consistent |
  4650	| a wrong ionisation limit | every term value shifts together |
  4651	| a mislabelled parent | the whole channel moves as one |
  4652	
  4653	 **Each is a complete index of something that is not there, and each was caught by a number the index could not supply** — a quantum defect of 4.9, a term value below zero.
  4654	
  4655	    Self-consistency detects an isolated error and certifies a systematic one. That is the whole
  4656	    case for requiring a second route that reaches outside, and it is narrower and sharper than "an index
  4657	    cannot check itself."
  4658

 Racah's recoupling coefficients translate between them exactly.

 **ⅅ_gro is the one with no instance anywhere until now.** *q*, this book's transfer coordinate, has
 no referent in the spectroscopic literature — not conflated, since there is nothing to conflate
 with. ⅅ_ref cannot see it: if no theorem names the term, the pair never enters the table.

 **And the three repairs are already named, in the companion paper, without being named as
 defences**: SPLIT for a conflation, DICTIONARY for one meaning in two bases, TRANSLATOR for a
 referent that must be manufactured. Register 403.

### 16.6.1 The vocabulary of reference, as an index

 The three new mechanisms need a vocabulary this book does not have: its back-matter Index carries
 fifty-one terms and **not one of them says what a term points at**. Defined here on the same
 discipline as every other index in this book — ordered coordinates, one categorical fibre,
 constraints of §16.4 form.

  coordinate   values
  access       blocked < secondary < abstract < full text
  referent     none < named < named with its stated hypothesis
  checked      not checked < against one theorem < against every theorem naming it
  verdict      undetermined < conflated < partial < match

 fibred by **kind** — coordinate · equation · source · result. *Repair* — none, dictionary, split,
 translator — is **not a coordinate**: it is a function of verdict and referent, and §17.2's Theorem 17.1
 forbids one — adjunction never repairs. It is read off.

 **38 cells, ambient box 144, density 26.4%, E = 0** — the densest object in this book after the
 periodic table. **And it is not a tree**: access bounds *referent at its top value* and bounds
 *checked* directly, closing the cycle access–referent–checked. Width 2, so Freuder cannot be
 inherited and the zero above is a computation rather than a certificate — §12.11.0.4's Λ₉′ arriving
 in the vocabulary rather than in the lattice.

 **Applied to twenty-eight load-bearing terms of this book and its companion: thirteen cells
 occupied of thirty-eight, E = 11.** One term with no referent, eight named and never checked, nine
 checked and conflated, two partial, eight matching, four capped by a blocked source. **Sixty-eight
 per cent have been checked at all.**

 **One constraint was withdrawn during construction and the withdrawal is the finding.** The index
 first required a named referent to have a reachable source, and refused four cells the book
 occupies — Edlén 1964, Ritz 1908, Paschen & Götze 1922, Dunz 1911. §19.5 already says otherwise:
 *a blocked ρ = 1 cell is a stated gap, not an unexplained absence.* Naming a referent and reading
 one are different acts. Totality forbade rather than detected, exactly as §16.5 says it does, and
 what it forbade located the wrong constraint. Register 404.

### 16.6.2 And one coordinate sits below this book's own floor

 §16.1 gives ⅅ ≥ 1 as the condition under which an index can check itself, and every defence in this
 book rests on it. **The reference index has one coordinate for which ⅅ = 0, permanently.**

 Three of its four coordinates are internal: *access*, *referent* and *checked* are all recordable
 from this book's own pages. **Verdict is not.** It requires reading someone else's theorem, and the
 index that supplies it is the bibliography — for which §29.1 already proves ⅅ(novelty) = 0,
 necessarily and permanently, because search is one route and can never be two.

    ⅅ(bibliography) = 0 ⟹ ⅅ(verdict) = 0, inherited.

 **So the reference debt is not unpayable because sources are blocked.** Blocked access caps four of
 twenty-eight terms at a lower level. The undefendability of *verdict* caps all twenty-eight, and it
 is the first coordinate anywhere in this book below the ⅅ ≥ 1 floor the rest of Chapter 16 stands
 on. Register 405.

 **No mechanism catches another's class**, and this work supplied an instance of each.

### 16.7 Two kinds of absence, and one kind of lie
 An index can be wrong in two ways, and they are not alike. One it can detect by itself. The
 other it cannot detect at all.

### 16.7.1 A missing cell — and the index can tell whether the gap is real
 E(X) > 0 says the structure admits cells the collection does not hold. It does not say why, and
 there are two reasons:

    the gap is an artefact of the layout — a property of how the index was drawn the gap is a fact
    about the world — nothing occupies that cell because nothing can

 **And the index distinguishes them, by asking whether E is removable.**

| the periodic table | E |
|---|---|
| 18-column | **36** |
| 32-column | 106 |
| **Janet left-step** | **0** |

 **The same 118 elements. Order the blocks f, d, p, s and define the period by *n* + ℓ, and the defect vanishes.** So the 36 belong to the drawing.

 Now the same test on a catalogue where the absences are physical. Index the mean-motion
 resonances by (p, q), reduced, with the order p − q derived rather than made an axis, and give ℛ only
 the resonances that show structure in the asteroid belt:

| the belt | E |
|---|---|
| (*p*, *q*) | 2 |
| (order, *p*) | 1 |
| (*p*, order) | 1 |

    E is irreducible, and ℛ refuses all six absences outright — 0 of 6 admitted, against 36 of
    36 admitted for the periodic table.

 And the physics confirms what the index inferred without being told it. Every resonance of order
 ≤ 7 in the belt is occupied; every one of order ≥ 8 is empty. Thirteen of thirteen above the cut, zero

 of six below. Resonance strength enters at e^\|p−q\|, so the absences are exponentially weak and
 genuinely unoccupied.

    A defect of the index vanishes under some re-coordinatisation. A feature of the world
    survives every one. The test is computable from the cells alone, and §6.2's Janet table is that test
    — run once, on one example, and never named as one.

### 16.7.2 A complete index of something that is not there
 The second failure is different in kind, and no re-coordinatisation touches it.

 Insert one impossible cell — **one electron with spin multiplicity 2, which no atom has** — and let the closure supply everything that follows. The result:

                                                                     Λ            the fabrication
  cells                                                              976          1,051
  closed under join and meet                                         true         true
  E(X)                                                               0            0
  fixed point of ℛ                                                   true         true

 **And E stays 0 for both under every re-coordinatisation tested.** The test of §16.7.1 has nothing to work on:

    that test finds missing cells and asks whether the gap is real. A coherent fabrication has
    no missing cells. It is full.

 **The fabrication contains 75 configurations no atom can have**, and the structure records nothing about it. Every law in this book certifies it.

### 16.7.3 The plain version
    A defective index is a map with a street missing. You catch it by redrawing — the street
    reappears in another projection. A coherent fabrication is a complete, consistent map of a
    city that does not exist. Every street connects, every distance adds up. Redrawing changes
    nothing, because nothing is missing.

 **The only thing that distinguishes a map of a real city from a perfect map of an imaginary one is going there.** In this book, going there means measuring a level.

### 16.7.4 Which is what D_phys is for, and only that
 §16.3's five recorded failures are all of the second kind. Not one is a missing cell.

| failure | what it does |
|---|---|
| a wrong nuclear charge | every derived value shifts **together**; the index stays consistent |
| a wrong ionisation limit | every term value shifts together |
| a mislabelled parent | the whole channel moves as one |

 **Each is a complete index of something that is not there, and each was caught by a number the index could not supply** — a quantum defect of 4.9, a term value below zero.

    Self-consistency detects an isolated error and certifies a systematic one. That is the whole
    case for requiring a second route that reaches outside, and it is narrower and sharper than "an index
    cannot check itself."

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# r2-ch13p.py — Phase R2, chat 85.  COMPUTABLE batch for the section read of main
# §16.6 through §16.8 (main L4482–L4788).  Every figure is re-measured on the rebuilt
# lattice; nothing is recited.  Deterministic: no wall-clock output, fixed seeds.
#
# Coordinate order at Λ₈ is (n, ℓ, k, q, e, f, g, 2S) — indices 0..7 — with
# min (1,0,1,0,1,0,0,0) and max (3,1,3,3,3,1,3,3) (MEASURED, chat 82).
#
# NEW, owed to r2lib (not lifted this build):
#   therm/untherm  — thermometer bit-packing of a cell into one uint32, under which
#                    coordinatewise join is bitwise OR and meet is bitwise AND.
#   lat_closure    — the join/meet sublattice generated by Λ ∪ {y}, by frontier.
#   Rtree          — the box sweep restricted to a given edge set (the "tree operator").
#   pushback       — J(x)+M(x), the pairs of other cells producing x.

import importlib.util, os, itertools, random
import numpy as np

H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', os.path.join(H, 'r2lib.py'))
r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(r2lib)
T = r2lib.load_tower()

NAMES = ['n', 'l', 'k', 'q', 'e', 'f', 'g', '2S']
IDX = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(NAMES)}
# the seven Heaviside constraints, as (bounded variable, bounding variable, printed form)
CONS = [('l', 'n', 'l <= n-1'), ('k', 'l', 'k <= 4l+2'), ('2S', 'k', '2S <= k'),
        ('q', 'k', 'q <= k'), ('g', 'q', 'g <= q'), ('g', 'f', 'g <= 4f+2'),
        ('f', 'e', 'f <= e-1')]
EDGES = sorted({tuple(sorted((IDX[a], IDX[b]))) for a, b, _ in CONS})

C8 = sorted(T.L8())
A8 = np.array(C8, dtype=np.int16)
LO, HI = A8.min(0), A8.max(0)
ALPHA = [list(range(int(LO[i]), int(HI[i]) + 1)) for i in range(8)]
BOX = [t for t in itertools.product(*ALPHA)]
S8 = set(C8)


def therm(t):
    v = 0
    for i, x in enumerate(t):
        v |= ((1 << (x + 1)) - 1) << (4 * i)
    return np.uint32(v)


def untherm(v):
    v = int(v)
    return tuple(bin((v >> (4 * i)) & 15).count('1') - 1 for i in range(8))


E8 = np.array([therm(t) for t in C8], dtype=np.uint32)


def lat_closure(y):
    """|sublattice generated by Λ₈ ∪ {y}|, y a thermometer code."""
    cells = np.append(E8, np.uint32(y))
    srt = np.unique(cells)
    front = np.array([np.uint32(y)], dtype=np.uint32)
    while len(front):
        o = np.bitwise_or(srt[None, :], front[:, None]).ravel()
        a = np.bitwise_and(srt[None, :], front[:, None]).ravel()
        u = np.unique(np.concatenate([o, a]))
        new = u[~np.isin(u, srt, assume_unique=True)]
        if not len(new):
            break
        srt = np.union1d(srt, new); front = new
    return len(srt)


def Rtree(X, edges):
    """ℛ restricted to a given edge set: Rset's sweep with phi kept only on those pairs."""
    A = np.array(sorted(set(X)), dtype=np.int64); d = A.shape[1]
    vals = [np.unique(A[:, i]) for i in range(d)]
    keep = set()
    for (i, j) in edges:
        keep.add((i, j)); keep.add((j, i))
    phi = {}
    for (i, j) in keep:
        m = np.full(int(A[:, j].max()) + 1, -1, dtype=np.int64)
        for v in vals[j]:
            m[v] = A[A[:, j] <= v, i].max()
        phi[(i, j)] = m
    G = np.array(np.meshgrid(*vals, indexing='ij')).reshape(d, -1).T
    ok = np.ones(len(G), dtype=bool)
    for (i, j), m in phi.items():
        ok &= G[:, i] <= m[G[:, j]]
    return set(map(tuple, G[ok]))


print('=== r2-ch13p — computable batch, main §16.6-§16.8 ===')
print('Λ₈ cells %d  alphabet %s  ambient box %d  candidates outside %d'
      % (len(C8), [len(a) for a in ALPHA], len(BOX), len(BOX) - len(C8)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. §16.8.1 L4665
# "φ(2S | k) = 1 at k = 1, the cell asks for 2, refused."
print('\n--- 1. §16.8.1 L4665: phi(2S | k) at k = 1 ---')
for kv in sorted({c[IDX['k']] for c in C8}):
    vs = sorted({c[IDX['2S']] for c in C8 if c[IDX['k']] == kv})
    print('   k = %d : admissible 2S = %s  phi = %d' % (kv, vs, len(vs)))
print('   printed: phi(2S|k) = 1 at k = 1')

# ------------------------------------------------- 2. §16.7.2 / §16.8.2 the fabrication
print('\n--- 2. §16.7.2 L4623-4627 / §16.8.2 L4670-4672: the fabrication ---')
Y = (1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 2)          # one electron (k = 1) asking 2S = 2
print('   inserted cell (n,l,k,q,e,f,g,2S) = %s   in Λ₈? %s' % (Y, Y in S8))
nfab = lat_closure(therm(Y))
print('   |Λ₈| = %d   |closure(Λ₈ ∪ {y})| = %d   A(y) = %d   new cells = %d'
      % (len(C8), nfab, nfab - len(C8) - 1, nfab - len(C8)))
# reconstruct the fabrication explicitly, check closure / E / fixed point
cells = np.unique(np.append(E8, therm(Y))); front = np.array([therm(Y)], dtype=np.uint32)
while len(front):
    o = np.bitwise_or(cells[None, :], front[:, None]).ravel()
    a = np.bitwise_and(cells[None, :], front[:, None]).ravel()
    u = np.unique(np.concatenate([o, a])); new = u[~np.isin(u, cells, assume_unique=True)]
    if not len(new): break
    cells = np.union1d(cells, new); front = new
FAB = sorted(untherm(v) for v in cells)
n2, jl, ml = r2lib.closure(FAB)
print('   fabrication closed under join/meet: joins outside %d, meets outside %d' % (jl, ml))
print('   E(fabrication) = |ℛ(X)| - |X| = %d' % (len(r2lib.Rset(FAB)) - len(FAB)))
print('   E(Λ₈)          = %d' % (len(r2lib.Rset(C8)) - len(C8)))
print('   fixed point of ℛ: fabrication %s   Λ₈ %s'
      % (set(r2lib.Rset(FAB)) == set(FAB), set(r2lib.Rset(C8)) == set(C8)))
bad = [c for c in FAB if c not in S8]
print('   cells the fabrication adds: %d   printed "75 configurations no atom can have"' % len(bad))
viol = {}
for c in bad:
    d = c[IDX['n']], c[IDX['l']], c[IDX['k']], c[IDX['q']], c[IDX['e']], c[IDX['f']], c[IDX['g']], c[IDX['2S']]
    t = []
    if d[1] > d[0] - 1: t.append('l<=n-1')
    if d[2] > 4 * d[1] + 2: t.append('k<=4l+2')
    if d[7] > d[2]: t.append('2S<=k')
    if d[3] > d[2]: t.append('q<=k')
    if d[6] > d[3]: t.append('g<=q')
    if d[6] > 4 * d[5] + 2: t.append('g<=4f+2')
    if d[5] > d[4] - 1: t.append('f<=e-1')
    viol[tuple(t)] = viol.get(tuple(t), 0) + 1
print('   which constraint each added cell breaks: %s' % dict(viol))

# ---------------------------------------------------- 3. §16.8.4 amplification, population
print('\n--- 3. §16.8.4 L4692-4693 / L4703 / Fig 16.2 L4714-4715: A over the population ---')
cand = [t for t in BOX if t not in S8]
Acode = {}
for t in cand:
    Acode[t] = lat_closure(therm(t)) - len(C8) - 1
vals = np.array(sorted(Acode.values()))
print('   population = every cell of the ambient box outside Λ₈: %d insertions' % len(vals))
print('   A: min %d  median %d  mean %.1f  max %d  zero-cost insertions %d'
      % (vals.min(), int(np.median(vals)), vals.mean(), vals.max(), int((vals == 0).sum())))
print('   printed body L4692-4693: "median of 340 ... minimum 59 across 220 trials, zero exceptions"')
print('   printed table L4703:     "amplifies, always - minimum 59"')
print('   printed Fig 16.2 L4714:  "over 140 random insertions ... median 352, minimum 15"')
for q in (0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95):
    print('     quantile %.2f = %d' % (q, int(np.quantile(vals, q))))
print('   cells with A < 59: %d   with A < 15: %d' % (int((vals < 59).sum()), int((vals < 15).sum())))
# single-constraint violators only (the population the per-constraint table implies)
single = {}
for t in cand:
    d = t
    t2 = []
    if d[1] > d[0] - 1: t2.append('l <= n-1')
    if d[2] > 4 * d[1] + 2: t2.append('k <= 4l+2')
    if d[7] > d[2]: t2.append('2S <= k')
    if d[3] > d[2]: t2.append('q <= k')
    if d[6] > d[3]: t2.append('g <= q')
    if d[6] > 4 * d[5] + 2: t2.append('g <= 4f+2')
    if d[5] > d[4] - 1: t2.append('f <= e-1')
    if len(t2) == 1:
        single.setdefault(t2[0], []).append(Acode[t])
sv = np.array(sorted(v for L in single.values() for v in L))
print('   restricted to cells breaking exactly ONE constraint (%d insertions):' % len(sv))
print('     A: min %d  median %d  mean %.1f  max %d' % (sv.min(), int(np.median(sv)), sv.mean(), sv.max()))
random.seed(1616)
for N in (140, 220):
    sm = [Acode[t] for t in random.sample(cand, N)]
    print('   a seeded random sample of %d: min %d median %d' % (N, min(sm), int(np.median(sm))))

# ------------------------------------------ 4. §16.8.4 L4721-4731 the descendants model
print('\n--- 4. §16.8.4 L4721-4729: descendants, fibre, and A/fibre ---')
succ = {v: set() for v in NAMES}
for a, b, _ in CONS:
    succ[b].add(a)                      # bounding -> bounded


def desc(v):
    seen, st = set(), [v]

        for w in succ[u]:

                seen.add(w); st.append(w)
    return seen

      % sorted((b, a) for a, b, _ in CONS))
print('   %-12s %-6s %-4s %s' % ('constraint', 'bound', 'desc', 'descendants'))
DESC = {}
for a, b, f in CONS:
    D = desc(a); DESC[f] = len(D)
    print('   %-12s %-6s %-4d %s' % (f, a, len(D), sorted(D)))
print('   printed L4726-4729: 2S<=k, g<=q, g<=4f+2 -> 0 ; q<=k, f<=e-1 -> 1 ; k<=4l+2 -> 3 ; l<=n-1 -> 4')
# fibre: the number of values the widened bound admits for the bounded variable
print('   %-12s %6s %8s %10s %10s' % ('constraint', 'n_ins', 'medA', 'fibre', 'A/fibre'))
rows = []
for f, L in sorted(single.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])):
    a = [c for c, b, ff in CONS if ff.replace(' ', '') == f.replace(' ', '')][0]
    fib = len(ALPHA[IDX[a]])
    med = float(np.median(L))
    rows.append((f, DESC[f.replace(' ', '')] if f.replace(' ', '') in DESC else DESC[f], med, fib, med / fib))
    print('   %-12s %6d %8.1f %10d %10.3f' % (f, len(L), med, fib, med / fib))

print('   corr(descendants, A/fibre) = %.3f   (printed -0.942)' % float(np.corrcoef(d, af)[0, 1]))
pred = 0.972 - 0.154 * d
err = np.abs(pred - af) / np.abs(af)
print('   printed model A ~ fibre x (0.972 - 0.154 d): median rel. error %.1f%%, worst %.1f%%'
      % (100 * float(np.median(err)), 100 * float(err.max())))
print('   printed L4722: "median error 7%, worst 24%"; L4731: "root is off by a factor of 2.5"')

# ------------------------------------------------- 5. §16.8.4 L4710 the rival bound
print('\n--- 5. §16.8.4 L4710: g <= 4f+2, the only constraint sharing its variable ---')
from collections import Counter
cnt = Counter(a for a, b, _ in CONS)
print('   bounded variables and how many constraints bound each: %s' % dict(cnt))
print('   variables bounded more than once: %s' % [v for v, c in cnt.items() if c > 1])
noriv = [c for c in BOX if not (c[1] > c[0] - 1 or c[2] > 4 * c[1] + 2 or c[7] > c[2]

n = len(E8)
pairs = n * (n - 1) // 2
print('   unordered pairs of distinct cells of Λ₈ = %d  (printed 475,800)' % pairs)
iu = np.triu_indices(n, 1)
J = np.bitwise_or(E8[iu[0]], E8[iu[1]])
Mt = np.bitwise_and(E8[iu[0]], E8[iu[1]])
pos = {int(v): i for i, v in enumerate(E8)}
push = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64)
for arr in (J, Mt):
    idx = np.array([pos[int(v)] for v in arr], dtype=np.int64)
    # a pair produces x only when neither member IS x
    keep = (E8[iu[0]] != arr) & (E8[iu[1]] != arr)
    np.add.at(push, idx[keep], 1)
print('   pushback J(x)+M(x): min %d  median %d  mean %.1f  max %d  cells with 0: %d'
      % (push.min(), int(np.median(push)), push.mean(), push.max(), int((push == 0).sum())))
print('   printed: minimum 16, median 504, mean 739, maximum 5,091, 0 removable')
jr = set(range(n)); mr = set(range(n))
jp = set(int(v) for v in np.unique(J)); mp = set(int(v) for v in np.unique(Mt))
ji = [i for i in range(n) if int(E8[i]) not in jp or True]
join_irr = [i for i in range(n) if not any(int(E8[i]) == int(v) for v in np.unique(J))]
meet_irr = [i for i in range(n) if not any(int(E8[i]) == int(v) for v in np.unique(Mt))]
print('   join-irreducible cells (not a join of two others): %d' % len(join_irr))
print('   meet-irreducible cells (not a meet of two others): %d' % len(meet_irr))
print('   intersection: %d   (printed "eighteen of each ... their intersection is empty")'
      % len(set(join_irr) & set(meet_irr)))
print('   cells with pushback 0: %s' % sorted(untherm(E8[i]) for i in range(n) if push[i] == 0))
print('   the least-pushed cell: %s at %d' % (untherm(E8[int(push.argmin())]), int(push.min())))

# ------------------------------------------------- 7. §16.8.5 L4755-4766 the step
print('\n--- 7. §16.8.5 L4755-4766: the sublattice theorem and step(Λ₈) ---')
n2, jl, ml = r2lib.closure(C8)
print('   Λ₈ closed under join and meet: joins outside %d, meets outside %d' % (jl, ml))
# distributivity of a product of chains, inherited: check on a seeded sample of triples
random.seed(4755); ok = True
for _ in range(20000):
    a, b, c = (random.choice(C8) for _ in range(3))
    l1 = tuple(min(max(a[i], b[i]), max(a[i], c[i])) for i in range(8))
    l2 = tuple(max(a[i], min(b[i], c[i])) for i in range(8))
    if l1 != l2: ok = False; break
print('   distributive on 20,000 seeded triples: %s' % ok)
JI = set(join_irr); MI = set(meet_irr)
best = None
for ai in JI:
    a = untherm(E8[ai])
    for bi in MI:
        b = untherm(E8[bi])
        if any(a[i] > b[i] for i in range(8)): continue
        iv = [c for c in C8 if all(a[i] <= c[i] <= b[i] for i in range(8))]
        rest = [c for c in C8 if c not in set(iv)]
        if not rest: continue
        R = np.array([therm(c) for c in rest], dtype=np.uint32); rs = set(int(v) for v in R)
        oo = np.bitwise_or(R[:, None], R[None, :]).ravel(); aa = np.bitwise_and(R[:, None], R[None, :]).ravel()
        fail = sum(1 for v in np.unique(np.concatenate([oo, aa])) if int(v) not in rs)
        if fail == 0 and (best is None or len(iv) < best[0]):
            best = (len(iv), a, b, len(rest))
print('   smallest removable interval [a,b] with a join-irr, b meet-irr and the rest a sublattice:')
print('     step = %s  a = %s  b = %s  cells left = %s' % (best[0], best[1], best[2], best[3]))
print('     printed: step(Λ₈) = 4, interval (2,1,3,3,2,1,3,0) to (3,1,3,3,3,1,3,0), 972 cells left')
if best:
    free = [NAMES[i] for i in range(8) if best[1][i] != best[2][i]]
    print('     free coordinates of the interval: %s   (printed "n and e")' % free)
    m = best[3]; print('     surviving pairs = %d  (printed 471,906)' % (m * (m - 1) // 2))

# ----------------------------------------- 8. §16.8.6 L4773-4787 the two operators
print('\n--- 8. §16.8.6 L4773-4787: binding pairs, transitive reduction, two operators ---')
bind = []
for i in range(8):
    for j in range(8):
        if i == j: continue
        mx = {}
        for c in C8: mx[c[j]] = max(mx.get(c[j], -1), c[i])
        vs = sorted(mx)
        if any(mx[vs[t]] != mx[vs[-1]] for t in range(len(vs))):
            bind.append((NAMES[j], NAMES[i]))
print('   ordered binding pairs (bound_j actually limits i): %d  (printed "16 binding coordinate pairs, not 7")'
      % len(bind))
print('   they are: %s' % sorted(bind))
red = [(b, a) for a, b, _ in CONS]
tc = set()
for u in NAMES:
    for w in desc(u):
        tc.add((u, w))
print('   transitive closure of the 7 defining edges: %d ordered pairs' % len(tc))
print('   equals the measured binding set: %s' % (set(bind) == tc))
print('   transitive reduction of the binding set returns %d edges: %s'
      % (len(red), sorted(red)))
print('   undirected constraint graph is a tree: %s (8 nodes, %d edges)'
      % (r2lib.is_tree(8, EDGES), len(EDGES)))
print('   %-12s %10s %12s' % ('constraint', 'A full', 'A tree-only'))
for f in ('l <= n-1', 'k <= 4l+2', '2S <= k'):
    a = [c for c, b, ff in CONS if ff == f.replace(' ', '')][0] if False else None
    ys = [t for t in cand if t in set(x for x in cand)]
    L = single.get(f, [])
    reps = [t for t in cand if True]
    # take the single-constraint violators of f and measure both operators on each
    vio = []
    for t in cand:
        t2 = []
        if t[1] > t[0] - 1: t2.append('l <= n-1')
        if t[2] > 4 * t[1] + 2: t2.append('k <= 4l+2')
        if t[7] > t[2]: t2.append('2S <= k')
        if t[3] > t[2]: t2.append('q <= k')
        if t[6] > t[3]: t2.append('g <= q')
        if t[6] > 4 * t[5] + 2: t2.append('g <= 4f+2')
        if t[5] > t[4] - 1: t2.append('f <= e-1')
        if t2 == [f]: vio.append(t)
    full = [len(r2lib.Rset(C8 + [t])) - len(C8) - 1 for t in vio[:40]]
    tre = [len(Rtree(C8 + [t], EDGES)) - len(C8) - 1 for t in vio[:40]]
    print('   %-12s %10s %12s   (n=%d shown of %d)'
          % (f, '%d/%d' % (min(full), max(full)), '%d/%d' % (min(tre), max(tre)), len(full), len(vio)))
print('   printed L4780-4782: l<=n-1 119 / 307 ; k<=4l+2 269 / 563 ; 2S<=k 74 / 74')
print('   ℛ_full(Λ₈) == Λ₈: %s   ℛ_tree(Λ₈) == Λ₈: %s'
      % (set(r2lib.Rset(C8)) == S8, set(Rtree(C8, EDGES)) == S8))

# --------------------------------------- 9. §16.6.1 L4537 the reference index
print('\n--- 9. §16.6.1 L4527-4546: the reference index, 38 cells / box 144 / E = 0 ---')
AX = {'access': 4, 'referent': 3, 'checked': 3, 'verdict': 4}
print('   printed coordinates and value counts: %s   product = %d'
      % (AX, 4 * 3 * 3 * 4))
print('   printed "38 cells, ambient box 144, density 26.4%%, E = 0"; 38/144 = %.4f' % (38 / 144))
print('   printed "thirteen cells occupied of thirty-eight, E = 11"')
print('   printed breakdown of 28 terms: 1 no referent + 8 named-never-checked + 9 conflated'
      ' + 2 partial + 8 matching = %d' % (1 + 8 + 9 + 2 + 8))
print('   printed "sixty-eight per cent have been checked at all": (28-1-8)/28 = %.4f' % (19 / 28))
# sweep every monotone reading of the stated constraints on (access, referent, checked, verdict)
found = []
Aa, Rr, Cc, Vv = range(4), range(3), range(3), range(4)
cells = [(a, r, c, v) for a in Aa for r in Rr for c in Cc for v in Vv]
import itertools as it
def mono(f, dom, rng):
    return all(f[i] <= f[j] for i in range(len(dom)) for j in range(len(dom)) if i <= j)
maps_ar = [m for m in it.product(range(3), repeat=4) if all(m[i] <= m[i + 1] for i in range(3))]
maps_ac = [m for m in it.product(range(3), repeat=4) if all(m[i] <= m[i + 1] for i in range(3))]
maps_vc = [m for m in it.product(range(4), repeat=3) if all(m[i] <= m[i + 1] for i in range(2))]
maps_vr = [m for m in it.product(range(4), repeat=3) if all(m[i] <= m[i + 1] for i in range(2))]
hits = []
for mar in maps_ar:
    for mac in maps_ac:
        for mvc in maps_vc:
            X = [(a, r, c, v) for (a, r, c, v) in cells
                 if r <= mar[a] and c <= mac[a] and v <= mvc[c]]
            if len(X) == 38:
                Xs = set(X)
                e = len(r2lib.Rset(X)) - len(X) if X else -1
                if e == 0:
                    hits.append((mar, mac, mvc, len(X), e))
print('   readings of "access bounds referent, access bounds checked, verdict bounded by checked"'
      ' giving exactly 38 cells with E = 0: %d of %d swept'
      % (len(hits), len(maps_ar) * len(maps_ac) * len(maps_vc)))
for h in hits[:6]:
    print('     access->referent %s  access->checked %s  checked->verdict %s' % h[:3])
print('   printed L4538-4539: "it is not a tree ... closing the cycle access-referent-checked"')
print('   the two constraints named at L4538-4539 (access->referent, access->checked) span'
      ' 3 nodes with 2 edges: cycle requires a third edge among them.')

print('\n=== end r2-ch13p ===')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# r2-ch13p.py — Phase R2, chat 85.  COMPUTABLE batch for the section read of main
# §16.6 through §16.8 (main L4482–L4788).  Every figure is re-measured on the rebuilt
# lattice; nothing is recited.  Deterministic: no wall-clock output, fixed seeds.
#
# Coordinate order at Λ₈ is (n, ℓ, k, q, e, f, g, 2S) — indices 0..7 — with
# min (1,0,1,0,1,0,0,0) and max (3,1,3,3,3,1,3,3) (MEASURED, chat 82).
#
# NEW, owed to r2lib (not lifted this build):
#   therm/untherm  — thermometer bit-packing of a cell into one uint32, under which
#                    coordinatewise join is bitwise OR and meet is bitwise AND.
#   lat_closure    — the join/meet sublattice generated by Λ ∪ {y}, by frontier.
#   Rtree          — the box sweep restricted to a given edge set (the "tree operator").
#   pushback       — J(x)+M(x), the pairs of other cells producing x.

import importlib.util, os, itertools, random
import numpy as np

H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', os.path.join(H, 'r2lib.py'))
r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(r2lib)
T = r2lib.load_tower()

NAMES = ['n', 'l', 'k', 'q', 'e', 'f', 'g', '2S']
IDX = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(NAMES)}
# the seven Heaviside constraints, as (bounded variable, bounding variable, printed form)
CONS = [('l', 'n', 'l <= n-1'), ('k', 'l', 'k <= 4l+2'), ('2S', 'k', '2S <= k'),
        ('q', 'k', 'q <= k'), ('g', 'q', 'g <= q'), ('g', 'f', 'g <= 4f+2'),
        ('f', 'e', 'f <= e-1')]
EDGES = sorted({tuple(sorted((IDX[a], IDX[b]))) for a, b, _ in CONS})

C8 = sorted(T.L8())
A8 = np.array(C8, dtype=np.int16)
LO, HI = A8.min(0), A8.max(0)
ALPHA = [list(range(int(LO[i]), int(HI[i]) + 1)) for i in range(8)]
BOX = [t for t in itertools.product(*ALPHA)]
S8 = set(C8)


def therm(t):
    v = 0
    for i, x in enumerate(t):
        v |= ((1 << (x + 1)) - 1) << (4 * i)
    return np.uint32(v)


def untherm(v):
    v = int(v)
    return tuple(bin((v >> (4 * i)) & 15).count('1') - 1 for i in range(8))


E8 = np.array([therm(t) for t in C8], dtype=np.uint32)


def lat_closure(y):
    """|sublattice generated by Λ₈ ∪ {y}|, y a thermometer code."""
    cells = np.append(E8, np.uint32(y))
    srt = np.unique(cells)
    front = np.array([np.uint32(y)], dtype=np.uint32)
    while len(front):
        o = np.bitwise_or(srt[None, :], front[:, None]).ravel()
        a = np.bitwise_and(srt[None, :], front[:, None]).ravel()
        u = np.unique(np.concatenate([o, a]))
        new = u[~np.isin(u, srt, assume_unique=True)]
        if not len(new):
            break
        srt = np.union1d(srt, new); front = new
    return len(srt)


def Rtree(X, edges):
    """ℛ restricted to a given edge set: Rset's sweep with phi kept only on those pairs."""
    A = np.array(sorted(set(X)), dtype=np.int64); d = A.shape[1]
    vals = [np.unique(A[:, i]) for i in range(d)]
    keep = set()
    for (i, j) in edges:
        keep.add((i, j)); keep.add((j, i))
    phi = {}
    for (i, j) in keep:
        m = np.full(int(A[:, j].max()) + 1, -1, dtype=np.int64)
        for v in vals[j]:
            m[v] = A[A[:, j] <= v, i].max()
        phi[(i, j)] = m
    G = np.array(np.meshgrid(*vals, indexing='ij')).reshape(d, -1).T
    ok = np.ones(len(G), dtype=bool)
    for (i, j), m in phi.items():
        ok &= G[:, i] <= m[G[:, j]]
    return set(map(tuple, G[ok]))


print('=== r2-ch13p — computable batch, main §16.6-§16.8 ===')
print('Λ₈ cells %d  alphabet %s  ambient box %d  candidates outside %d'
      % (len(C8), [len(a) for a in ALPHA], len(BOX), len(BOX) - len(C8)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. §16.8.1 L4665
# "φ(2S | k) = 1 at k = 1, the cell asks for 2, refused."
print('\n--- 1. §16.8.1 L4665: phi(2S | k) at k = 1 ---')
for kv in sorted({c[IDX['k']] for c in C8}):
    vs = sorted({c[IDX['2S']] for c in C8 if c[IDX['k']] == kv})
    print('   k = %d : admissible 2S = %s  phi = %d' % (kv, vs, len(vs)))
print('   printed: phi(2S|k) = 1 at k = 1')

# ------------------------------------------------- 2. §16.7.2 / §16.8.2 the fabrication
print('\n--- 2. §16.7.2 L4623-4627 / §16.8.2 L4670-4672: the fabrication ---')
Y = (1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 2)          # one electron (k = 1) asking 2S = 2
print('   inserted cell (n,l,k,q,e,f,g,2S) = %s   in Λ₈? %s' % (Y, Y in S8))
nfab = lat_closure(therm(Y))
print('   |Λ₈| = %d   |closure(Λ₈ ∪ {y})| = %d   A(y) = %d   new cells = %d'
      % (len(C8), nfab, nfab - len(C8) - 1, nfab - len(C8)))
# reconstruct the fabrication explicitly, check closure / E / fixed point
cells = np.unique(np.append(E8, therm(Y))); front = np.array([therm(Y)], dtype=np.uint32)
while len(front):
    o = np.bitwise_or(cells[None, :], front[:, None]).ravel()
    a = np.bitwise_and(cells[None, :], front[:, None]).ravel()
    u = np.unique(np.concatenate([o, a])); new = u[~np.isin(u, cells, assume_unique=True)]
    if not len(new): break
    cells = np.union1d(cells, new); front = new
FAB = sorted(untherm(v) for v in cells)
n2, jl, ml = r2lib.closure(FAB)
print('   fabrication closed under join/meet: joins outside %d, meets outside %d' % (jl, ml))
print('   E(fabrication) = |ℛ(X)| - |X| = %d' % (len(r2lib.Rset(FAB)) - len(FAB)))
print('   E(Λ₈)          = %d' % (len(r2lib.Rset(C8)) - len(C8)))
print('   fixed point of ℛ: fabrication %s   Λ₈ %s'
      % (set(r2lib.Rset(FAB)) == set(FAB), set(r2lib.Rset(C8)) == set(C8)))
bad = [c for c in FAB if c not in S8]
print('   cells the fabrication adds: %d   printed "75 configurations no atom can have"' % len(bad))
viol = {}
for c in bad:
    d = c[IDX['n']], c[IDX['l']], c[IDX['k']], c[IDX['q']], c[IDX['e']], c[IDX['f']], c[IDX['g']], c[IDX['2S']]
    t = []
    if d[1] > d[0] - 1: t.append('l<=n-1')
    if d[2] > 4 * d[1] + 2: t.append('k<=4l+2')
    if d[7] > d[2]: t.append('2S<=k')
    if d[3] > d[2]: t.append('q<=k')
    if d[6] > d[3]: t.append('g<=q')
    if d[6] > 4 * d[5] + 2: t.append('g<=4f+2')
    if d[5] > d[4] - 1: t.append('f<=e-1')
    viol[tuple(t)] = viol.get(tuple(t), 0) + 1
print('   which constraint each added cell breaks: %s' % dict(viol))

# ---------------------------------------------------- 3. §16.8.4 amplification, population
print('\n--- 3. §16.8.4 L4692-4693 / L4703 / Fig 16.2 L4714-4715: A over the population ---')
cand = [t for t in BOX if t not in S8]
Acode = {}
for t in cand:
    Acode[t] = lat_closure(therm(t)) - len(C8) - 1
vals = np.array(sorted(Acode.values()))
print('   population = every cell of the ambient box outside Λ₈: %d insertions' % len(vals))
print('   A: min %d  median %d  mean %.1f  max %d  zero-cost insertions %d'
      % (vals.min(), int(np.median(vals)), vals.mean(), vals.max(), int((vals == 0).sum())))
print('   printed body L4692-4693: "median of 340 ... minimum 59 across 220 trials, zero exceptions"')
print('   printed table L4703:     "amplifies, always - minimum 59"')
print('   printed Fig 16.2 L4714:  "over 140 random insertions ... median 352, minimum 15"')
for q in (0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95):
    print('     quantile %.2f = %d' % (q, int(np.quantile(vals, q))))
print('   cells with A < 59: %d   with A < 15: %d' % (int((vals < 59).sum()), int((vals < 15).sum())))
# single-constraint violators only (the population the per-constraint table implies)
single = {}
for t in cand:
    d = t
    t2 = []
    if d[1] > d[0] - 1: t2.append('l <= n-1')
    if d[2] > 4 * d[1] + 2: t2.append('k <= 4l+2')
    if d[7] > d[2]: t2.append('2S <= k')
    if d[3] > d[2]: t2.append('q <= k')
    if d[6] > d[3]: t2.append('g <= q')
    if d[6] > 4 * d[5] + 2: t2.append('g <= 4f+2')
    if d[5] > d[4] - 1: t2.append('f <= e-1')
    if len(t2) == 1:
        single.setdefault(t2[0], []).append(Acode[t])
sv = np.array(sorted(v for L in single.values() for v in L))
print('   restricted to cells breaking exactly ONE constraint (%d insertions):' % len(sv))
print('     A: min %d  median %d  mean %.1f  max %d' % (sv.min(), int(np.median(sv)), sv.mean(), sv.max()))
random.seed(1616)
for N in (140, 220):
    sm = [Acode[t] for t in random.sample(cand, N)]
    print('   a seeded random sample of %d: min %d median %d' % (N, min(sm), int(np.median(sm))))

# ------------------------------------------ 4. §16.8.4 L4721-4731 the descendants model
print('\n--- 4. §16.8.4 L4721-4729: descendants, fibre, and A/fibre ---')
succ = {v: set() for v in NAMES}
for a, b, _ in CONS:
    succ[b].add(a)                      # bounding -> bounded


def desc(v):
    seen, st = set(), [v]
    while st:
        u = st.pop()
        for w in succ[u]:
            if w not in seen:
                seen.add(w); st.append(w)
    return seen


print('   directed dependency edges (bounding -> bounded): %s'
      % sorted((b, a) for a, b, _ in CONS))
print('   %-12s %-6s %-4s %s' % ('constraint', 'bound', 'desc', 'descendants'))
DESC = {}
for a, b, f in CONS:
    D = desc(a); DESC[f] = len(D)
    print('   %-12s %-6s %-4d %s' % (f, a, len(D), sorted(D)))
print('   printed L4726-4729: 2S<=k, g<=q, g<=4f+2 -> 0 ; q<=k, f<=e-1 -> 1 ; k<=4l+2 -> 3 ; l<=n-1 -> 4')
# fibre: the number of values the widened bound admits for the bounded variable
print('   %-12s %6s %8s %10s %10s' % ('constraint', 'n_ins', 'medA', 'fibre', 'A/fibre'))
rows = []
for f, L in sorted(single.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])):
    a = [c for c, b, ff in CONS if ff.replace(' ', '') == f.replace(' ', '')][0]
    fib = len(ALPHA[IDX[a]])
    med = float(np.median(L))
    rows.append((f, DESC[f.replace(' ', '')] if f.replace(' ', '') in DESC else DESC[f], med, fib, med / fib))
    print('   %-12s %6d %8.1f %10d %10.3f' % (f, len(L), med, fib, med / fib))
d = np.array([r[1] for r in rows], dtype=float); af = np.array([r[4] for r in rows])
print('   corr(descendants, A/fibre) = %.3f   (printed -0.942)' % float(np.corrcoef(d, af)[0, 1]))
pred = 0.972 - 0.154 * d
err = np.abs(pred - af) / np.abs(af)
print('   printed model A ~ fibre x (0.972 - 0.154 d): median rel. error %.1f%%, worst %.1f%%'
      % (100 * float(np.median(err)), 100 * float(err.max())))
print('   printed L4722: "median error 7%, worst 24%"; L4731: "root is off by a factor of 2.5"')

# ------------------------------------------------- 5. §16.8.4 L4710 the rival bound
print('\n--- 5. §16.8.4 L4710: g <= 4f+2, the only constraint sharing its variable ---')
from collections import Counter
cnt = Counter(a for a, b, _ in CONS)
print('   bounded variables and how many constraints bound each: %s' % dict(cnt))
print('   variables bounded more than once: %s' % [v for v, c in cnt.items() if c > 1])

input.description: Replace the 32-bit lookup table with a compact mixed-radix index (thermometer codes exceed addressable range)
input.old_str:
order = {int(v): i for i, v in enumerate(E8)}
lut = np.zeros(int(E8.max()) + 1, dtype=np.int64)
for v, i in order.items(): lut[v] = i
push = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64)
for arr in (J, Mt):
    keep = (E8[iu0] != arr) & (E8[iu1] != arr)
    np.add.at(push, lut[arr[keep]], 1)
input.new_str:
POP = np.array([bin(x).count('1') - 1 for x in range(16)], dtype=np.int64)
WR = np.cumprod(np.concatenate(([1], (HI[:-1] + 1).astype(np.int64))))
NBOX = int(np.prod(HI + 1))


def rad_idx(arr):
    """thermometer codes -> compact mixed-radix index (popcount per nibble = coordinate value)."""
    out = np.zeros(len(arr), dtype=np.int64)
    for i in range(8):
        out += POP[(arr >> np.uint32(4 * i)) & np.uint32(15)] * WR[i]
    return out


lut = np.full(NBOX, -1, dtype=np.int64)
lut[rad_idx(E8)] = np.arange(n)
push = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64)
for arr in (J, Mt):
    keep = (E8[iu0] != arr) & (E8[iu1] != arr)
    np.add.at(push, lut[rad_idx(arr[keep])], 1)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# r2-ch13q.py — Phase R2, chat 85.  PROSE batch for the section read of main §16.6–§16.8
# (main L4482–L4788): self-counts, pointers resolved to the claim, restated figures,
# attributions, citation chains and vocabulary.  Deterministic; no wall-clock output.

import re, collections

D = '/home/claude/members/'
F = {'main': 'The_Method_1_6-2.md', 'reg': 'The_Method_1_6___The_Register-2.md',
     'mc': 'The_Method_1_6___Mathematical_Compendium-2.md',
     'pc': 'The_Method_1_6___The_Physics_Compendium-2.md',
     'ioi': 'The_Method_1_6___The_Index_of_Indices-2.md',
     'sc': 'The_Method_1_6___Spectra_Compendium-2.md'}
L = {k: open(D + v, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n') for k, v in F.items()}
M, R = L['main'], L['reg']
A, B = 4482, 4788
SEC = M[A - 1:B]


def sites(pat, vols=None, flags=0):
    out = []
    for k in (vols or F):
        for i, l in enumerate(L[k], 1):
            if re.search(pat, l, flags): out.append((k, i))
    return out


def show(k, i, w=118):
    return L[k][i - 1].strip()[:w]


print('=== r2-ch13q — prose batch, main §16.6-§16.8 (L%d-L%d, %d lines) ===' % (A, B, B - A + 1))

# ------------------------------------------------- 1. §16.6's self-count
print('\n--- 1. §16.6 L4482: "The defences are disjoint, and there are six" ---')
t1 = [i for i in range(4483, 4487) if M[i - 1].strip()]
t2 = [i for i in range(4491, 4499) if M[i - 1].strip()]
print('   first table L4483-4486  : header + %d mechanism rows' % (len(t1) - 1))
for i in t1[1:]: print('      L%d %s' % (i, show('main', i, 70)))
print('   second table L4491-4498 : header + %d mechanism rows' % (len(t2) - 1))
for i in t2[1:]: print('      L%d %s' % (i, show('main', i, 90)))
print('   L4488 says: %s' % show('main', 4488))
print('   L4489 says: %s' % show('main', 4489))
print('   L4500 says: %s' % show('main', 4500))
print('   heading count "six" ; second table rows %d ; L4500 "first four ... last three" = %d'
      % (len(t2) - 1, 4 + 3))
print('   L4572: %s' % show('main', 4572))

# ------------------------------------------------- 2. restated figures elsewhere
print('\n--- 2. figures of §16.6 restated elsewhere ---')
for pat, tag in ((r'[Tt]wenty-one structural audits', 'twenty-one structural audits'),
                 (r'ⅅ_gro', 'D_gro'), (r'ⅅ_ref', 'D_ref'), (r'ⅅ_dict', 'D_dict'),
                 (r'multiverse', 'multiverse'), (r'fifty-one terms|51 terms', 'fifty-one terms'),
                 (r'TRANSLATOR', 'TRANSLATOR'), (r'DICTIONARY', 'DICTIONARY')):
    s = sites(pat)
    print('   %-26s %d site(s): %s' % (tag, len(s), s[:8]))

# ------------------------------------- 3. the DEFERRED item: multiverse dimension / D_gro
print('\n--- 3. DEFERRED (chats 74, 83, 84): §16.6 L4482 "multiverse dimension ⅅ_gro" ---')
print('   §14.6.1 L4115: %s' % show('main', 4115))
print('   §14.6.1 L4116: %s' % show('main', 4116))
print('   occurrences of "multiverse" inside §16.6 (L4482-4519): %d'
      % sum(1 for l in M[4481:4519] if 'multiverse' in l))
print('   occurrences of "multiverse" in the whole main volume: %d'
      % sum(1 for l in M if 'multiverse' in l))
print('   what §16.6 actually grades with ⅅ_gro:')
for i in (4498, 4512, 4513, 4514):
    print('      L%d %s' % (i, show('main', i)))
print('   §29.2.2 opens L7922: %s' % show('main', 7922))
print('   "not posable" in main: %s' % sites(r'not posable', ['main'])[:6])

# ------------------------------------------------- 4. pointers resolved to the claim
print('\n--- 4. every §-pointer in range, resolved to the CLAIM ---')
CHECK = [
    (4495, '§28.8', 7721, r'index'),
    (4525, '§16.4', 1765, r'monotone function of one other'),
    (4534, '§17.2', 4806, r'adjunction never repairs'),
    (4540, '§12.11.0.4', 2725, r'separation hypothesis'),
    (4550, '§19.5', 5432, r'blocked|stated gap|ρ'),
    (4552, '§16.5', 4449, r'totality'),
    (4557, '§16.1', 4335, r'counting argument'),
    (4562, '§29.1', 7859, r'novelty'),
    (4615, '§6.2', 1594, r'Janet'),
    (4629, '§16.7.1', 4578, r'missing cell'),
    (4645, '§16.3', 4359, r'wrong value in the data'),
    (4683, '§2.13', 649, r'Commit before you look'),
    (4734, '§16.8.4', 4691, r'cost of a fabrication'),
    (4786, '§11', 2075, r'single expression'),
]
for src, ptr, head, pat in CHECK:
    end = head
    while end + 1 < len(M) and not re.match(r'^#{2,4} ', M[end]):
        end += 1
    body = '\n'.join(M[head - 1:end])
    hit = len(re.findall(pat, body, re.I))
    print('   L%-5d %-12s -> L%-5d  "%s" occurs %d time(s) in that section  %s'
          % (src, ptr, head, pat[:34], hit, 'OK' if hit else '**ZERO**'))
print('   §19.5, the exact phrase §16.6.1 attributes to it:')
print('     §16.6.1 L4551: %s' % show('main', 4551))
for p in (r'stated gap', r'unexplained absence', r'ρ = 1'):
    print('     "%s" in main: %s' % (p, sites(p, ['main'])[:6]))
print('   §6.2 Janet: %s' % sites(r'Janet', ['main'])[:10])

        print('      L%d %s' % (i, show('main', i, 100)))

for i in range(4647, 4652):
    if M[i - 1].strip(): print('      L%d %s' % (i, show('main', i, 100)))
print('   L4653: %s' % show('main', 4653))
for p in (r'term value below zero', r'below zero'):

Section read under the chat-81 cadence: the whole section read first, its claims censused into

**Boundaries, MEASURED by heading scan before reading:** §16.6 opens **L4482**; Chapter 17 opens

§16.7.1–§16.7.4 (L4578, L4618, L4636, L4644), §16.8 (L4659), §16.8.1–§16.8.6 (L4663, L4669, L4683,
